newsitem.title: SPAIN: Iberia to secure alliance by summer.
newsitem.headline: Iberia to secure alliance by summer.

text.p: Spain's state-owned airline Iberia will secure an international alliance before the summer with two partners, one American and one European, state holding company SEPI, which controls Iberia, said on Monday.
SEPI said American Airlines and Continental Airlines remained in the running.

"Iberia will have two partners, one American and one European, and both will have a small, symbolic shareholding (in Iberia)," a SEPI spokesman confirmed, responding to comments made by chairman Pedro Ferreras in local media.

SEPI said the American partner would also take a 20 percent stake in troubled airline Aerolineas Argentinas. Iberia will maintain its 20 percent stake and the remainder will be sold off to private investors.
"With this, we will solve our Latin America problem as far as Aerolineas is concerned...we did not get there in time for Ladeco and Viasa," Pedro Ferreras told magazine Dinero.
Chilean airline Ladeco said at the beginning of April that Iberia would sell its 38 percent stake in the carrier.
Shareholders in Venezuela's Viasa last month agreed to liquidate the airline within a year, after various attempts to save the loss making carrier. Iberia holds a 45 percent stake in the airline.

SEPI's Ferreras said: "There is the group formed by American Airlines and British Airways and another of Continental Airlines and Air France...the American partner could be either of those....and the European partner could be entirely separate," Ferreras said.
Netherlands' airline KLM, for example, could be a candidate, he said.
But he added that the world of international airline alliances was very precarious, and Iberia was keeping all its doors open and continuing talks with a range of airlines.
Under the terms of the alliance, the two partners will take up to a five percent stake in Iberia. "The stake will just be symbolic. What we are really interested in is the project," Ferreras said.
After the alliance, SEPI said it would then look for other private investors to take stakes in the airline. The privatisation of Iberia could take place around 1999, Ferreras said.
An Iberia source said in March the airline was in continuing talks with British Airways, but that a deal was pending a European Commission decision on BA's link-up with AMR Corp's American Airlines.
